checker writes the regenerated result to /tmp, so the archived output file itself was not changed.Zero-cost 2SAT auditLet  $s_i=1$  mean that operation  $i$  is selected. For a fixed distinct replacement list  $(x_i,y_i)$ , with  $x_i\in U$  and  $y_i\notin U$ ,
$$\operatorname{present}(x_i)=1-s_i,\qquad
\operatorname{present}(y_i)=s_i.$$
Every other vertex has a constant membership value:vertices in  $U$  that are not removed are constantly present;vertices outside  $U$  that are not added are constantly absent.For an ambient edge  $\{a,b\}$ , zero matching cost is equivalent to forbidding simultaneous presence:
$$\neg\bigl(\operatorname{present}(a)\land\operatorname{present}(b)\bigr).$$
The implementation handles every case correctly.If either endpoint is constantly absent, the edge constraint is vacuous.If both endpoints are constantly present, the generated clause is empty and the instance is unsatisfiable.If one endpoint is constantly present and the other requires  $s_i=p$ , the result is a unit prohibition.If both endpoints are variable, the result is a two-requirement prohibition.If the same operation occurs at both ends of an edge, the requirements are  $(i,0)$  and  $(i,1)$ . They are complementary and cannot be simultaneously true, so the edge constraint is tautological.Duplicate requirement entries are removed before clause construction.A technical point that was checked explicitly is that sat() does not receive ordinary CNF literals. It receives requirements of the form “ $s_i=p$ ” and interprets each clause as:
$$\text{forbid all listed requirements simultaneously}.$$
For a two-requirement clause  $(a,b)$ , it adds the implications
$$a\Rightarrow \neg b,\qquad b\Rightarrow \neg a,$$
which is exactly the implication graph for  $\neg a\lor\neg b$ . A one-requirement clause is duplicated internally, producing the correct unit implication  $a\Rightarrow\neg a$ .The SCC assignmentPythonvalues = [int(label[2*v+1] > label[2*v]) for v in range(variables)]was checked against the exhaustive assignment controls and against the final clause assertion. When a variable and its complement lie in the same SCC, the checker verifies two directed contradiction paths: $2v\to 2v+1$  $2v+1\to 2v$ Every path hop is checked against the constructed implication graph. The corresponding clauses are separately checked against actual uncovered ambient edges through clause_edges, so the obstruction is tied back to the graph rather than being an abstract SAT artifact.The checker recorded:14,468 edge-clause truth controls over all assignments,1,472 constant/empty-clause obstructions,1,662 SCC contradiction paths.I also ran a supplemental exhaustive check of the internal zero-cost reduction on 5,039 arbitrary simple-graph instances through four vertices, including graphs outside the public validator’s bipartite maximum-degree-two domain. The SAT feasibility result agreed with direct enumeration of every operation subfamily in all cases.Therefore the graph-general mathematical statement is correct: the zero-cost equivalence itself does not require bipartiteness or a degree bound.Positive threshold auditFor a selected batch  $S$ , let
$$H_S=A[U_S]$$
be the final induced graph. On the validated bipartite domain, König’s theorem gives
$$\nu(H_S)\le B
\iff
\tau(H_S)\le B
\iff
\exists Z\subseteq V(A),\ |Z|\le B,\ H_S-Z\text{ is independent}.$$
The implementation enumerates every ambient vertex subset  $Z$  of size at most  $B$ . For each such  $Z$ , it discards edges incident with  $Z$  and invokes the same 2SAT construction on the remaining edges.The two directions are implemented correctly.From a low-cost batch to an enumerated exception setIf  $\nu(H_S)\le B$ , bipartite matching/vertex-cover duality supplies a vertex cover  $Z'\subseteq U_S$  with  $|Z'|\le B$ . The enumeration includes  $Z'$ , and  $U_S-Z'$  is independent, so its 2SAT instance is satisfiable.From a satisfiable enumerated set to a low-cost batchIf the 2SAT instance for an ambient set  $Z$  is satisfiable, the resulting batch has no final edge with both endpoints outside  $Z$ . Therefore
$$Z\cap U_S$$
is a vertex cover of  $H_S$ . Its size is at most  $|Z|\le B$ , so the final matching number is at most  $B$ .The code deliberately allows enumerated  $Z$  to contain vertices absent from the final membership set. It then returnsPythonfinal_cover = set(covered) & set(cert['U'])and asserts that this intersection covers every final edge. This is the correct treatment of ambient exception sets.The final certificate routine returns an actual matching and cover on the induced degree-two bipartite graph. The checker verifies:the matching edges are actual final induced edges;matching edges are vertex-disjoint;matching size equals the reported actual cost;cover size equals matching size;every final induced edge meets the returned cover;the returned exception cover is contained in the final present set;its size is at most  $B$ .The checker recorded 8,373 positive witnesses and 850 fully exhausted failed cover searches.Complexity classificationThe implementation tests at most

exception sets, with one polynomial-size SCC computation per set. Hence the shipped algorithm is in XP with respect to  $B$ : for each fixed  $B$ , the running time is polynomial in the graph and list size, with an exponent depending on  $B$ .The note correctly makes no FPT claim of the form
